issues.on_page: 4700 Building Improvements - Purchased Property Services 270,000.00 (p25); Depreciation Fund '5200 Allocation from General Fund' 270,000.00 (p16)
issues.issue: Transfer cross-check fails inside detail. The receiving side (detail[30], Depreciation 5200 Allocation from General Fund, +270,000) is recorded as other financing, so it is treated as a transfer in. The sending side (General Fund 4700 Building Improvements) stays as an expenditure (capital outlay / land and buildings) with no matching -270,000 other financing line. Account code 5200 is the same code the Activities (p17) and School Nutrition (p18) schedules print as 'Transfers From General Fund', so this is an interfund transfer. As entered, the same money counts as spending in General and as a transfer in Depreciation. Record both sides the same way: either both as transfers (-270,000 other financing in General, with split_from/review) or both as revenue/spending.

issues.on_page: Building Improvements 270,000.00 (General Fund column p7, Total p8); Depreciation Non-Revenue Receipts 270,000.00 (p5)
issues.issue: The 270,000 General-to-Depreciation allocation (code 5200, a transfer) is counted as governmental spending (capital outlay) here and as revenue in receipts[13] Non-Revenue Receipts (276,721.10 = 6,721.10 General + 270,000.00 Depreciation, by column on p5/p6). The statement itself carries it as a receipt/disbursement and shows no elimination, and the extractor raised it in decision_needed. Under the transfer rules, though, it inflates both receipts and disbursements by 270,000 (net effect on cash is zero). It needs a decision before the totals are used.

issues.on_page: State Programs 37,456.33 = 3535 High Ability Learners 8,456.33 + 3551 Career Education 7,500.00 + 3552 School Safety and Security 21,500.00 (p25)
issues.issue: Mixed line. Its largest part (School Safety and Security, 21,500 = 57%) is support services, and detail[167] records it that way. The rules say to use the dominant category, so this would be support services. It currently conflicts with the detail.
County-distributed fines and license fees. 'fines and forfeitures' would also be defensible; this is a judgment call.

'Purchased Property Services' gets different categories across the report: repairs and maintenance (2510, 2620, 2670, 2730, 3552), utilities (2610, detail[138]), land and buildings (4700) and professional/contract services here. Depreciation-fund property services are more likely repairs and maintenance.
